subject: Post-call: FinEx throughput & latency SLO qualification
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finex.com>, Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: FinEx throughput & latency SLO qualification

Hi Oliver / Sofia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery focused on performance and SLOs so we can size the Dedicated offering and propose a canary: 

- Goal SLOs: p95 latency <= 250ms for streaming responses (important for chat UX).
- Traffic profile: mix of session-based chat and async batch reranking.
- Key missing inputs for sizing: steady-state QPS, peak QPS, average tokens per request, concurrency (simultaneous sessions), % of requests that need streaming, and any strict burst windows.

Next steps (proposal):
1) Please fill the attached throughput template with per-endpoint numbers and sample tokens-per-request (we left a sample row).
2) If convenient, export a 24–72h sample of production traffic (anonymized) and share the CSV — fields: timestamp, endpoint, tokens_in, tokens_out, success/fail, request_id.
3) We’ll run a quick estimation and propose a Dedicated configuration + recommended batching/quantization profile and an initial canary plan (48-hour test window).

Questions I had after the call:
- Do you have hard concurrency limits per user session?
- For streaming: do you require server-sent events (chunked) or are client-side polling websockets okay?

I’ve attached our throughput template to make it quick — cc’ing Marissa and Neha to jump in on the canary/CS side.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachment: redwood_throughput_template.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@finex.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 20:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinEx throughput & latency SLO qualification

Thanks Rafael — nice summary. Answers inline below and attached a small export that should help (anonymized).

- Steady-state QPS: ~20 QPS (mixed text-generation + embeddings).
- Peak QPS: ~120 QPS during end-of-day reconciliation windows (approx 10-15 minute bursts).
- Avg tokens per request: 900 tokens in / ~1200 tokens out for the chat endpoint; reranking requests are much smaller (~150 tokens).
- Concurrency: typical concurrent sessions ~150, but only ~20–25 actively streaming at the same time.
- Streaming: yes, streaming is required for chat front-end (server-sent chunking preferred).
- Latency target: p95 <= 250ms end-to-end for streaming messages (we understand there is some client-side processing), p50 target tighter ~120ms.

We attached a 48h sample export (filtered). Also flagged any PII — none included. Let us know if you need longer.

Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of Platform Engineering | FinEx
oliver.grant@finex.com

Attachment: finex_workload_export.csv (CSV stub)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finex.com>, Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinEx throughput & latency SLO qualification

Oliver — really helpful, thanks for the numbers and the export. A few clarifying items and a proposed plan: 

Clarifiers:
- When you say peak QPS ~120 for 10-15 minutes, is that a single global peak (all regions) or per-region?
- For streaming concurrency: the ~20–25 active streams — is that max observed or averaged during peaks?

Proposed immediate plan:
1) We’ll run a quick throughput estimate using your CSV + our template and come back with: expected GPUs, recommended q8_0 quantization profile for chat, expected tokens/sec, and estimated cost.
2) Canary: 48-hour window during a non-business-critical window — we propose 2 m5d-sized Dedicated nodes (we’ll provide exact GPU SKU after initial calc) with continuous batching enabled and streaming optimizations. We’ll set circuit-breaker fallbacks and an auto-fallback to a lighter model variant if latency climbs >300ms for >5 minutes.
3) Test traffic: can FinEx open a test API key or proxy that we can hit from our Dedicated environment for an isolated canary? Alternatively, we can mirror a subset of traffic if you prefer.

Would Marissa / Neha be able to own the canary doc? I’ll draft an initial canary plan and share the doc (redwood_canary_plan.md) for your review.

Thanks — I’ll aim to get the initial sizing numbers to you by Monday morning.

—R
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@finex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinEx throughput & latency SLO qualification

Thanks Rafael — we can create a test API key and a small proxy in our staging VPC for the mirror. I'll share credentials with Neha directly (SFTP/secure channel) and we can agree on the test window: Tue 09/01 03:00–07:00 PDT (this maps to your low-traffic window).

Confirmed: peak 120 QPS is global (single region), active streams ~25 at peak. We’re happy to start with the 48-hour canary you proposed (we prefer it not to overlap with month-end reconcile windows).

Sofia Ramos
Senior PM, Product Ops | FinEx
sofia.ramos@finex.com
